### GSA/open-gsa-redesign — Subcontracting Plan Reports API
- URL: https://github.com/GSA/open-gsa-redesign
- Exact commit / revision: `494b1312e9c6436474840befe6e1964da15932b3`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender
- What it contains: Official GSA SAM.gov OpenAPI 3.1 schema for the modernized eSRS Subcontracting Plan Reports API. Search fields include UEI, ultimate-parent UEI, legal business name, PIID, referenced-IDV PIID, subcontract number, organization code, fiscal year/report type and reporting period; responses cover report, entity, contract, task-order, goals/actuals and certification data.
- Rare or undernoticed value: Official subcontracting-plan performance evidence that complements award/incumbent history with contract lineage and small-business-goal/actual reporting context.
- Likely buyer / user: GovCon capture/BD teams, primes, subcontractors, supplier-diversity/compliance groups and consultants.
- Painful problem: Award history alone does not show a prime's subcontracting-plan performance or tie those reports cleanly to PIID/referenced-IDV/UEI lineage.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Add an authorized incumbent-subcontracting evidence section to CaptureBrief packets for customers that already have required SAM.gov System Account access.
- Build-time / data advantage: Roughly 2-4 months of official schema/access/field-semantics and contract-lineage discovery avoided.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact revision; `_apidocs/spr-api/v1/openapi.yaml` with System Account security, UEI/parent-UEI/PIID/referenced-IDV filters and report/contract/entity/task-order/goals/certification schemas; repository public-domain/CC0 notice.
- License / rights: Official U.S. government work; repository licensing provides public-domain/CC0 reuse. Actual report access is permissioned and requires authorized System Account credentials/API key.
- Reuse classification: Schema/documentation reusable under stated rights; production data access must stay inside authorized SAM.gov permissions.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Valuable schema is buried inside a broad GSA redesign repository rather than a standalone procurement-data project.
- Score: **29/30** — A4, B5, C5, D5, E5, F5.
- Combination opportunities: DATA Act identity + USAspending award history + SPR PIID/referenced-IDV/goals-actuals + mcp-sam-gov clause/deviation evidence.
- Next action: Add optional SPR evidence to the 10-live-solicitation benchmark and require explicit unresolved state when customer access is absent.

- Combination opportunities: Portal adapter -> raw/hash snapshot -> Kingfisher/OCDS normalization -> CaptureBrief packet.

### bedrocka-ventures/bedrocka-tools-calc
- URL: https://github.com/bedrocka-ventures/bedrocka-tools-calc
- Exact commit / revision: `7723112b433f6ca9351bddaf0c37248e673356db`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: rejected / unsafe as current GovCon eligibility authority
- What it contains: MIT deterministic SBA size-standard calculator/checker.
- Why rejected: Inspected federal-contracting receipts logic uses a three-year average and user-supplied thresholds. Current 13 CFR §121.104 generally uses the most recent five completed fiscal years for firms in business five or more years, subject to program-specific exceptions, and affiliate receipts matter. Stale deterministic logic is riskier than an unresolved state.
- License / rights: MIT.
- Value score: **15/30** — A2, B3, C3, D2, E3, F2 for safe present reuse.
- Next action: Do not use its eligibility result path; use versioned official SBA/eCFR rules with effective dates and explicit exception/affiliation handling.
